userStories.title: Fix a2e-projects install-time workspace-schema build failure — relation target has no object metadata (object-metadata-with-relations-gql-object-type.generator.ts:117)
userStories.description: As an operator installing A2E Suite, I want a2e-projects to install cleanly on a live server so that M1a provisioning reaches 6/6 registered apps, P4.1's live validation and human-ID concurrency proof become runnable, and the a2e-chat dependency chain unblocks.
acceptanceCriteria: PLAN anchor (phase-01-report 2026-09-22 15:25, verbatim): "a2e-projects 0.1.0 install FAILS at install-time workspace-schema build: `Field Metadata of type RELATION or MORPH_RELATION with id <ephemeral> has no relation target object metadata` from `object-metadata-with-relations-gql-object-type.generator.ts:117`. The failing field id differs every retry and never persists (clean rollback); the manifest is statically self-consistent (all relation targets resolve within the manifest or standard objects); the same schema builds fine outside install. **Genuine code defect (case a):** install-time schema build orders/collects object+field metadata such that freshly-inserted relation fields can run through the generator before their target object is visible to it. Fix direction: collect the full object+field set before running the generators (or resolve relation targets from the manifest rather than re-querying). Recorded for the executor queue."

Reproduce at the exact cited site first: packages/twenty-server/src/engine/api/graphql/workspace-schema-builder/graphql-type-generators/object-types/object-metadata-with-relations-gql-object-type.generator.ts:117 throws "Field Metadata of type RELATION or MORPH_RELATION with id <id> has no relation target object metadata" — the failing field is an EPHEMERAL (in-flight, not-yet-persisted) relation field whose relationTargetObjectMetadataId points at an object that is not present in the SchemaGenerationContext's flatObjectMetadataMaps at generation time

Trace the install-time call path and fix the ordering/collection defect where it lives (expected chain: workspace-graphql-schema-sdl.service.ts getOrComputeSchemaSDL → gql-type.generator.ts buildAndStoreObjectMetadataGqlTypes per-object loop at line 86-126, which calls objectMetadataWithRelationsGqlObjectTypeGenerator.buildAndStore per object with only the CURRENT object's fields resolved from flatFieldMetadataMaps) — per the phase report's fix direction, either collect the full object+field set (including in-flight/ephemeral relation targets from the applying manifest) before running the generators, or resolve relation targets from the manifest rather than re-querying the not-yet-committed maps; do NOT fix it by weakening the line-117 guard, deleting the error, or hard-coding a2e-projects identifiers — the guard stays and must still fire for genuinely unresolvable targets

The fix must be generic to ANY app install (not a2e-projects-specific): the same manifest shape (relation fields targeting other objects in the same manifest, e.g. task→project, milestone→project, timeEntry→task) is what every internal app ships; a regression test must construct exactly the reported condition — a relation field whose target object metadata is absent from the context maps — and assert the schema builds via the manifest-declared target instead of throwing

Existing behavior preserved: the same schema build OUTSIDE install (normal workspace-schema generation on committed metadata) must keep producing byte-identical SDL — rerun the workspace-schema-builder unit suites (packages/twenty-server/src/engine/api/graphql/workspace-schema-builder/**) plus the metadata workspace-migration/flat-entity suites adjacent to the touched path and confirm no assertion changed

If the defect turns out to live in how install-time install flushes/passes flatEntityMaps to the schema generator (e.g. workspace-migration build+run handing pre-flush maps), fix it there instead and record the corrected root-cause chain in the report entry — either way the acceptance proof is a failing-then-passing test at the reported condition, not a speculative reorder

Do NOT touch a2e-projects app source (packages/twenty-apps/internal/a2e-projects/**) — the phase report states the manifest is statically self-consistent and the same schema builds fine outside install; the defect is in the server's install-time generator path

Live install re-proof is the orchestrator's leg (Tier 2): report entry must name it as the residual (per phase-01-report: M1a a2e-projects install leg + phase-04-report: P4.1 'Concurrency proof deferred until that defect is fixed')

userStories.title: Fix CRM nav-restore defect — template apply unconditionally skips the navigation step when the hide-list is empty, so STUDENT-deleted CRM nav rows are never restored (workspace-template.service.ts:392-401)
userStories.description: As a workspace owner switching a workspace from a persona template back to CRM, I want the CRM apply to actually restore the CRM navigation rows a previous persona apply deleted, matching what the CRM preview advertises (restore×3), so that switching templates is reversible as the C2 contract requires.
acceptanceCriteria: PLAN anchor (phase-01-report 2026-09-22 15:25, verbatim): "**DEFECT:** STUDENT apply hard-deletes CRM nav rows (`20202020-b001/b004/b005-…`); a later CRM apply NEVER restores them because the navigation-visibility step in `workspace-template.service.ts` (`runRemainingSteps`) unconditionally skips when the definition's `hiddenStandardNavigationMenuItemUniversalIdentifiers` is empty — while CRM's own preview advertises restore×3. Fix: drive the nav step from current row state (restore missing TEMPLATE_MANAGED rows even with an empty hide-list), not from the definition. Workspace state restored by hand (SQL, rows re-created from the YC template with Apple's own applicationId/metadata ids) after the probe; defect left unfixed per the Tier-2 no-fix rule."

Reproduce at the exact cited site first: packages/twenty-server/src/engine/core-modules/onboarding/workspace-template.service.ts:392-401 — runRemainingSteps checks `isNonEmptyArray(definition.hiddenStandardNavigationMenuItemUniversalIdentifiers)` and marks the navigation-visibility step 'skipped' when empty, so a CRM apply (hide-list []) never calls applyTemplateNavigationVisibility; note the restore machinery BELOW the skip is already correct (workspace-template.service.ts:851-856 computes universalIdentifiersToRestore from TEMPLATE_MANAGED_STANDARD_NAVIGATION_MENU_ITEM_UNIVERSAL_IDENTIFIERS minus hidden minus existing rows, and buildStandardNavigationMenuItemsToRestore rebuilds them) — the defect is purely the premature skip, not the migration builder

Fix: remove the unconditional hide-list-based skip in runRemainingSteps (lines 392-401) so the navigation-visibility step always invokes applyTemplateNavigationVisibility; drive restoration from current workspace row state inside applyTemplateNavigationVisibility, exactly as the phase report directs — applyTemplateNavigationVisibility must keep its existing no-op early return (lines 858-863: nothing to delete AND nothing to restore) so a fresh CRM workspace applies without a needless migration; do NOT delete or weaken that no-op path

Preview/apply consistency: the fix restores exactly what the preview advertises — workspace-template.service.ts:674-690 (navigationChanges: hide = definition hide-list, restore = TEMPLATE_MANAGED rows not in the hide-list) is the contract the apply step must satisfy for EVERY template, including CRM (hide×0 + restore×3); add/extend a spec asserting preview navigationChanges and the apply step's resulting create/delete migration agree for CRM, individual (hide×3) and at least one more persona

C2 contract regression tests (unit, mocked workspaceCacheService + validateBuildAndRunWorkspaceMigration like the existing suites): (a) workspace whose flatNavigationMenuItemMaps are missing TEMPLATE_MANAGED rows (the post-STUDENT state) + CRM apply → validateBuildAndRunWorkspaceMigration called with flatEntityToCreate carrying the missing rows' universal identifiers (20202020-b001/b004/b005-… per the live probe) and navigation-visibility step 'succeeded'; (b) same missing rows + CRM apply AGAIN (now restored) → no migration call, step 'succeeded' (or the existing no-op semantics), idempotent re-run; (c) CRM apply on a fresh complete workspace → no migration call (no-op early return preserved); (d) individual apply → existing hide behavior from workspace-template.service.spec.ts:701-738 unchanged

The existing suites must stay green unchanged in their assertions: workspace-template.service.spec.ts ('leaves navigation untouched for the CRM template' at :740 currently asserts validateBuildAndRunWorkspaceMigration NOT called for CRM — on a COMPLETE workspace this stays true under the no-op early return; update its setup only if it relied on the premature skip rather than the no-op, and record that in the report), plus idempotency (:379-483), partial-failure and apply-template-operation-fixtures suites

Do NOT touch template definitions (hiddenStandardNavigationMenuItemUniversalIdentifiers stay as-is — CRM legitimately hides nothing) and do NOT implement user-hidden-item preservation here (PLAN C2's 'restore only what it hid, not user-hidden navigation' is a separate acceptance; if the fix exposes that gap, record it in the report entry as a flagged defect for a separate slice, exactly as the orchestrator did for these two)

Live verification is the orchestrator's leg (Tier 2): report entry must name the residuals — a live STUDENT-apply → CRM-apply probe (the exact sequence the defect was found with, now safe to run after US-075) and the P1.3/P1.6c/E03 browser legs, which stay deferred per tasks/deferred-batch9.md
